Loading a session's settings saves them straight back. `chat.js:384` calls `vc.load_grouped(...)`, and `load_overrides` emits `"change"` on every row it touches (`core/Plugin/Plugin.js:75,87`). The handler wired at `chat.js:260-273` hears that and POSTs, so opening or switching to a session appends a redundant `{"settings":…}` line to its `session.jsonl`. A load must not write: mute `save_plugins` while `load_grouped` runs.

Settings can be saved to the wrong session. The 400 ms timer in `chat.js:266-271` reads `owner.ctl.session` and `vc.overrides` when it fires, not when the change happened. Change a slider in session A, then switch to B within 400 ms while `Session.get(B)` is still in flight: A's overrides are appended to B's `session.jsonl`. Capture the session id when the change happens, and cancel the timer on switch.

Servex's `group_plugins` (`Servex/agents/Sessions.js:259-270`) re-does `VoiceChat.overrides_by_group()` (`VoiceChat.js:23`), which no production code calls (only tests). To do it, Servex imports the browser's `ux/Dictate/VoiceChat` and its plugins at startup, so a broken plugin file now takes Servex down. `plugins_of` (`Sessions.js:425`) reads and replays the whole `session.jsonl`, chat included, on every GET and on every debounced settings POST. That is fine for now; on a long voice session it is a full replay per slider move. A small "last settings line" scan would do the same job.

When a session opens, the browser's remembered barge-in values (`Interrupt.snapshot`, `chat.js:260`) are now replaced by the session's settings. For every existing session that is `{}`, so the remembered threshold silently stops applying. That may be intended ("a new session starts from the defaults"), but nowhere says so; one line in `ux/Dictate/doc/settings.md` would.

`plan.md:100` (the step 4 Status line) still says "the page always posts the whole current `vc.overrides` (flat), and Servex does the group split". That is the opposite of what landed in 4cc9405ea: the page splits, and Servex refuses a flat object. The line also leaves out the fix commit and the next step, so a fresh agent reading the plan would be misled. Rewrite it: one splitter in the browser, commits e9ddafafe + 4cc9405ea, next is step 5.

`ext/Session/Session.js` (the new `settings` export's doc comment) says `plugins` is "same shape VoiceChat.overrides gives: {Name: {enabled?, config?}}". Servex now rejects that shape with a 400 (`checked_plugin_groups`). It must say `{dictate, recite}`, from `vc.overrides_by_group()`. Only `get()` returns the flat shape.

`ux/Dictate/VoiceChat/readme.md:27` ("Watch out") still says "The bar's own controls still save to the browser until the settings are saved with the session". Settings are saved with the session now. `ux/Dictate/doc/settings.md` sends readers to this "Watch out" for the rule that an open session replaces the browser's remembered barge-in values, but that rule isn't there. Update the line to state it.

`ux/Dictate/chat.js` (`attach()`, the `Session.get(...).then`) has no check that the session is still the current one when the reply arrives. If you switch sessions quickly, the older reply can arrive last and load the previous session's settings into the chat. The next change would then save them under the new session. A guard like `if (rec.id !== owner.ctl.session) return` (or capturing the id) closes it.

The save wiring runs once per page (`chat.js`, the `_settings_wired` block) and reads `owner` from the first mount's closure. `owner` is per mount when `keep` is false (`chat.js:186`). On a page with two mounts watching different sessions, a change saves under the first mount's session. `VoiceChat/readme.md` "Watch out" (one VoiceChat per page) says this is by design, but nothing says which session wins.
`chat.js` and `doc/settings.md` both name a `save_plugins` that no longer exists (it is the anonymous `"change"` handler now). Rename it in the text, or give the handler that name.

findings.text: Every edit made in the panel redraws the whole panel, so a slider stops after one step and a number box or dropdown loses focus. `PluginSettings.set` calls `row.set` first, and the row sends "change" straight away (core/Item/Item.js:327). The `watch()` listener (ux/Dictate/ChatSettings.js ~l.85) sees `this.own` still false, because `changed()` only sets it later, on the `ps.emit("change")` after that. Then `refresh()` → `fill()` swaps the slider out from under the pointer. Fix: set the guard before `row.set`, e.g. inside `PluginSettings.set`, or skip the refresh while the event comes from a panel row.

Send after's "when you pause" and "every two sentences" are not kept when you stop the mic. `stop()` calls `this.send_sentences()` (ext/Chat/Mic.js:788), whose default `n` reads `SETTINGS.sentences_per_send` (Mic.js:636) and ignores the mic's own value. So with "when you pause" the held words still go one sentence at a time, which breaks its promise in SendAfter.js ("everything goes as one message"). With "two" they go one at a time. Read `this.sentences_per_send ?? SETTINGS…` there too, and add a test.

The interrupt slider still doesn't show which end does what at 360. In minion-settings-build-step5/panel-360-full.png, "any small sound counts as you" sits next to the label, the slider is on a line of its own, and "only loud talking counts as you" is on the line below. Neither text sits at its own end of the slider, and the owner specifically couldn't tell what this slider changed. Put `low` | slider | `high` on one line, or label the two ends under the slider.

With read-aloud off, the line goes from `sending` straight back to empty while the agent works. plan.md says this, so the next step can add the `stream` source the brief allowed for.

The comment at `ux/Dictate/chat.js:291` says "one ChatStatus per page", but the block runs once per `chat()` call. Each chat adds a `Recite.on` and a `floor.on_mic` listener that is never removed. `floor` is page-global, so a second chat on the same page would also show `listening` for the first chat's mic. This is harmless with one chat per page; the comment should say what actually happens.

The test command in `ux/Dictate/doc/settings.md` ("Status line", last line) is `node ux/Dictate/ChatStatus.test.mjs`. From the repo root it is `node public/framework/ux/Dictate/ChatStatus.test.mjs`, which is how the test file's own header says it.

The new `changed()` calls in `audio/Recite/Recite.js` (`expect_reply`, `start_thinking`, `cancel_cue`) also wake ReciteBubble's `sync()` and ReciteHighlight's `tick()`. Both are cheap redraws, and `cancel_cue` fires only when the value flips, but `audio/Recite/readme.md` doesn't say that `on()` now fires for the cue too.
